rows.definition: belief in one's own capacity to act effectively
rows.retire_reason: the only candidate instruments (business formation, quits) are already the instruments for perceived_control. Two constructs sharing one instrument set are one construct with two names

proxies.rationale: aggregate sentiment of public text; the weakest instrument here, and marked as such rather than given a flattering noise

rows.retire_reason: requires a licensed text corpus. A tone index built from whatever happens to be scrapeable measures the scrape

rows.definition: sense of connection to a community
rows.retire_reason: no public series measures it, and no behavioural proxy discriminates it from participation measures already used elsewhere
survey dispersion would be the right instrument and the public releases publish central tendencies, not distributions

confounders: news cycle drives stated sentiment independently of experience
delinquency is a lagging record of a decision made months earlier
partisan composition shifts survey levels without any change in behaviour
rows.definition: the degree to which households expect their own financial position to worsen, and act to protect against it
rows.expected_direction: rises with debt service burden and delinquency; falls with sentiment
rows.measurement_risk: the 2022 divergence — sentiment at recessionary levels while consumption held — is the standing evidence that the stated and revealed instruments here can disagree for years

proxies.rationale: consumer confidence indices fall when households report worry about their own finances; inverted because high confidence is low anxiety
households miss payments when they have run out of buffer; a behavioural record rather than a stated feeling
revolving credit growth outpacing income growth indicates borrowing to cover ordinary consumption
the share of the basket in staples rises when households protect against a worse month ahead
precautionary saving rises with anxiety -- but a high saving rate is equally consistent with perceived control, so this cannot discriminate on its own
the share of disposable income committed to debt service is the cleanest non-survey measure of how much room a household has left; unlike a sentiment index it cannot be moved by the news

confounders: the OECD indicator is itself partly built from national surveys this engine also reads, which is a lineage problem as much as a confounding one
rows.definition: whether households are oriented toward improvement ahead or toward protecting what they have
rows.expected_direction: rises with the OECD confidence indicator
rows.measurement_risk: LINEAGE: if the OECD indicator incorporates UMich, then using both is double counting. Marked and not yet resolved

proxies.rationale: discretionary purchase intent is deferred first when the future feels short
substituting cheaper alternatives is the first observable act of a shortened horizon
the OECD consumer confidence indicator is normalised around 100 and leads its own national surveys; used for orientation toward the future rather than for present anxiety

rows.retire_reason: would share every instrument with future_orientation; kept distinct in the vocabulary and retired here rather than given a duplicate loading

rows.definition: confidence that institutions will behave predictably and in good faith

proxies.rationale: published trust indices are the direct instrument, with all the framing sensitivity that survey instruments carry
confidence-in-institutions survey batteries

rows.retire_reason: the major trust barometers are proprietary and annual. An annual figure cannot support a quarterly-horizon forecast comparison, so even licensing one would not make this testable at the horizons this engine forecasts at

rows.definition: trust in other people rather than institutions
rows.retire_reason: the General Social Survey measures it biennially with a multi-year lag. Real, and far too slow for any horizon this engine forecasts at

confounders: quits rise in a hot labour market regardless of how anyone feels
participation falls for demographic reasons unrelated to control
rows.definition: the degree to which workers believe they can change their own situation through their own action
rows.expected_direction: rises with quits and participation; falls with involuntary underemployment
rows.measurement_risk: the quits rate is a labour-market statistic first and a psychological reading second; if it adds value, the value may belong to the labour market rather than to the construct

proxies.rationale: households who expect their own situation to improve report more command over it than those expecting only the economy to improve
voluntarily leaving a job is a costly signal that a worker believes they can secure another
the quits rate is the cleanest revealed-preference reading of workers' confidence in their own options
new business applications commit personal capital to a belief that effort will produce a result
involuntary part-time work is the absence of the outside option that makes a worker feel in command; weaker here than for security because it conflates 'cannot find' with 'chose not to look'

rows.definition: sense that outcomes are distributed justly
rows.retire_reason: no public series; the survey instruments that exist are annual, framing-sensitive and not released as time series

confounders: U-6 conflates 'could not find full-time' with 'chose part-time'
employment ratio moves with retirement demographics
rows.definition: a household's sense that its current position is stable, distinct from anxiety about the future
rows.expected_direction: rises with the employment-population ratio; falls with U-6 underemployment
rows.measurement_risk: security and control share the labour market as their evidence base and may not be separable in practice; they are kept apart because their instruments differ, and the incremental-value test will say whether that distinction earns anything

proxies.rationale: U-6 counts people working part-time because they could not find full-time work — involuntary underemployment is the direct observable of insecurity, distinct from anxiety about it
the share of the working-age population actually employed; a structural floor under a household's sense of its own position

confounders: the equity share rises mechanically when equities rise, with no change in behaviour — a valuation effect, not an allocation decision
rows.definition: households' willingness to hold volatile assets and take on future obligation
rows.expected_direction: rises with the household equity share
rows.measurement_risk: THE VALUATION CONFOUND IS SEVERE. A share-of-assets measure moves with prices. Any finding here must be checked against a flow measure before it means anything

proxies.rationale: the share of retail activity in the most speculative instruments available to households
aggregate household allocation to volatile assets
applying for credit commits to a future obligation -- though it also rises under distress, which is the opposite state
household equity holdings as a share of financial assets is revealed allocation, not stated intent

rows.definition: acute, near-term distress in the population

proxies.rationale: search volume for distress terms; a weak instrument because search behaviour is driven by news cycles as much as by experience

rows.retire_reason: search-volume series are the standard proxy and the trends APIs forbid the redistribution this would require. The alternative — distress-term frequency in public text — measures the news cycle, not the population

confounders: both instruments are rate-sensitive, and rates are in the base economic model already
durable orders include defence and aircraft, which are not household decisions at all
rows.definition: how far ahead households are willing to commit resources
rows.expected_direction: rises with durable-goods orders and home sales
rows.measurement_risk: the rate sensitivity means this construct may add nothing over a base model that already holds rates; that is exactly what the incremental-value test is for

proxies.rationale: intent to buy a durable good is a commitment to a horizon longer than the purchase itself
durable-goods orders and new-home sales commit a household to a horizon longer than the purchase; both are placed on a common scale by the proxy's declared range

rows.retire_reason: would share business formation with perceived_control and agency; retired rather than triple-counted
